title: Around town: autos, cabs & buses
goal: Get around Bhubaneswar and Cuttack on your own: agree an auto fare, give directions from the back seat, say 'stop here' and 'drop me at…', ask how long it takes, and handle a ride-app pickup.
intro:
In Odisha's cities you'll mostly move by **auto** (ଅଟୋ), app cab or bike taxi, and the blue city buses (*Mo Bus* in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack); there's no metro yet. Autos are either **ଶେୟାର୍** (shared, fixed route, cheap) or **ରିଜର୍ଭ୍** (hired just for you, fare agreed first). With autos and drivers you'll use the respectful **ଆପଣ** forms, but call them **ଭାଇ** 'brother'.

The grammar is what makes 'take me' and 'drop me' sound natural: **compound verbs**, where a helper like ଦେବା, ଯିବା or ନେବା follows the -ଇ form (ରଖି**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ** 'stop (for me)', ଓହ୍ଲାଇ**ଯିବି** 'I'll get off'), and the very handy **ଲାଗିବା** for time and money: କେତେ ସମୟ **ଲାଗିବ**? 'how long will it take?'

vocab.note: Talking about him: ଅଟୋବାଲା. Talking to him: ଭାଇ (or ଦାଦା / ମଉସା for an older man).
From English 'reserve'. ରିଜର୍ଭ୍ ଯିବେ? 'will you take me (alone, not shared)?'
ଶେୟାର୍ ଅଟୋ: runs a fixed route, picks up anyone, fixed small fare.
ମିଟରରେ 'by the meter'. Rarely used by Odisha autos; the fare is usually agreed first.

vocab.en: to drop (someone) off; to let go
vocab.note: ମୋତେ ଛକରେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ 'drop me at the junction'.

vocab.en: (to a driver) to stop, pull over; to put down
vocab.note: ଏଠି ରଖିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ 'stop here, please'. With ତୁମେ: ରଖିଦିଅ.
ଡ୍ରପ୍ କରିଦେବା 'to drop (someone) off', very common with friends: ମୋତେ ଡ୍ରପ୍ କରିଦେବୁ?
Causative of ପହଞ୍ଚିବା "to arrive": "to make arrive".

vocab.note: ଗାଡ଼ି ବୁଲାଅ 'turn the car around'; ସହର ବୁଲାଇବା 'to show someone the town'.

ଖାଲି ଅଟୋ 'an empty auto'; ଖାଲି ଦଶ ଟଙ୍କା 'only ten rupees'.
ଆପରେ ବୁକ୍ କରିବା 'to book on the app'.

grammar.title: Compound verbs: ରଖିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ, ଓହ୍ଲାଇଯିବି, କିଣିନେବି
grammar.body:
Odia often says an action with **two verbs**: the main verb in the **-ଇ form** + a **helper** that carries the tense and person. The helper adds a shade of meaning, and some combinations are simply how the thing is said.

**ଦେବା 'give'** — the action is done *for someone else*, or completely; in requests it sounds softer and friendlier: ରଖି**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ** 'stop (for me)', ଛାଡ଼ି**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ** 'drop me', ବୁଲାଇ**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ** 'turn round', ଡ୍ରପ୍ କରି**ଦେବୁ**? 'will you drop me?'
**ଯିବା 'go'** — completion, a change of state, or movement away: ଓହ୍ଲାଇ**ଯିବି** 'I'll get off', ପହଞ୍ଚି**ଗଲି** 'I've reached', ଫସି**ଗଲି** 'I got stuck', ଭୁଲି**ଗଲି** 'I forgot'.
**ନେବା 'take'** — done *for yourself*: କିଣି**ନେବି** 'I'll buy it (for myself)', ବୁକ୍ କରି**ନେବି** 'I'll book it myself'.
**ପଡ଼ିବା 'fall'** — sudden, unplanned: ଶୋଇ**ପଡ଼ିଲି** 'I fell asleep', ବସି**ପଡ଼ିଲା** 'he plonked himself down'.
**ଆସିବା 'come'** — movement towards: ଚାଲି**ଆସ** 'come over'.

Only the helper changes: ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବି, ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଲେ, ଛାଡ଼ିଦିଅ, ଛାଡ଼ିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ. Negatives usually drop the helper: 'don't drop me here' = ଏଠି ଛାଡ଼ନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ.

**Compare** the -ଇ form of Unit 22, which links *two separate* actions (ଅଟୋ **ନେଇ** ଆସ 'take an auto and come'). A compound is *one* action with a nuance. The giveaway: in a compound, you can't put 'and then' between the verbs.

grammar.title: 'It takes…': ଲାଗିବା for time (and ପଡ଼ିବା for cost)
grammar.body:
You met **ଲାଗିବା** as 'to feel' (ଭୋକ ଲାଗୁଛି). With an amount of time it means **'to take'**. The time is the subject, and the person (if you mention one) goes in the dative, just like ମୋତେ ଭୋକ ଲାଗୁଛି:

କେତେ ସମୟ **ଲାଗିବ**? — How long will it take?
ଅଧ ଘଣ୍ଟା **ଲାଗେ** — It takes half an hour (usually).
**ମୋତେ** ଦୁଇ ଘଣ୍ଟା **ଲାଗିଲା** — It took me two hours.

To say *what* takes the time, use the **-ବାକୁ** form: କଟକ **ଯିବାକୁ** ଘଣ୍ଟେ ଲାଗେ 'it takes an hour to get to Cuttack'.

**Money**: ଲାଗିବା works for cost too (ଶେୟାର୍ ଅଟୋରେ କୋଡ଼ିଏ ଟଙ୍କା ଲାଗେ), and **ପଡ଼ିବା** 'to come to, work out at' is very common for a total: ଭଡ଼ା କେତେ ପଡ଼ିବ? 'what will the fare come to?'

**Distance**: କେତେ ଦୂର? 'how far?' — ପାଞ୍ଚ କିଲୋମିଟର୍ 'five kilometres'.

**Trap**: don't use ନେବା 'take' for time. 'It takes an hour' is never 'ଘଣ୍ଟେ ନିଏ'. ନେବା is for the *driver* taking money: କେତେ ନେବେ? 'how much will you take?'

examples.native: ଏଠାରୁ ପୁରୀ ଯିବାକୁ କେତେ ସମୟ ଲାଗିବ?

examples.en: How long does it take to get to Puri from here?

examples.en: Because of the jam it took me an hour today.

culture:
Auto fares in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack are agreed **before** you get in: name the place, ask କେତେ ନେବେ?, offer a bit less, and if it's still too high, smile and walk to the next auto, which often brings the price down. Fares go up at night and in the rain, and drivers will ask more from people who look like visitors, so checking the app price first is the modern way to bargain (as Sam does). Once the fare is agreed, there's no tipping.

Address drivers as **ଭାଇ** (or ଦାଦା / ମଉସା if he's older) and use the polite -ନ୍ତୁ forms: ରଖିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ, ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ. Many locals use ତୁମେ with young drivers, but as a learner you can't go wrong with ଆପଣ. Directions run on landmarks, not street names: 'opposite the bank', 'behind the Hanuman temple', 'the lane after the petrol pump'. In Bhubaneswar, the blue **Mo Bus** city buses are cheap, air-conditioned on many routes and take UPI, and app cabs, autos and bike taxis are all on the usual ride apps. Between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, people take buses, trains or shared autos across the Mahanadi bridge.

tip.title: Haggling with an auto driver
tip.body:
- Name the place + **ଯିବେ?**: ଷ୍ଟେସନ ରିଜର୍ଭ୍ ଯିବେ?
- Ask the price: **କେତେ ନେବେ?** Counter: **ଏତେ ନୁହେଁ, … ଦେବି.**
- Call him **ଭାଇ** and use the -ବେ / -ନ୍ତୁ forms; agree the fare before you get in.

tip.title: Compound verbs: -ଇ + helper
tip.body:
- Main verb in **-ଇ**, helper carries the ending: ରଖି**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ**, ଛାଡ଼ି**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ**.
- **ଦେବା** = for someone / softer request · **ଯିବା** = completion, getting off (ଓହ୍ଲାଇ**ଯିବି**) · **ନେବା** = for yourself (କିଣି**ନେବି**) · **ପଡ଼ିବା** = sudden (ଶୋଇ**ପଡ଼ିଲି**).

tip.title: Steering the driver
tip.body:
- **ଟିକେ ଆଗକୁ** 'a bit further', **ପଛକୁ** 'back', **ସାମ୍ନାରେ** 'opposite'.
- Turn: **ଡାହାଣକୁ / ବାଁକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ**; 'at the lights' = **ସିଗନାଲରୁ**.
- Landmarks beat street names: ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ ସାମ୍ନାରେ, ମନ୍ଦିର ପଛରେ.

tip.title: ଲାଗିବା: it takes (time, money)
tip.body:
- Time is the subject of **ଲାଗିବା**: କେତେ ସମୟ **ଲାଗିବ**? · ଅଧ ଘଣ୍ଟା **ଲାଗେ**.
- The person goes in the dative: **ମୋତେ** ଘଣ୍ଟେ ଲାଗିଲା 'it took me an hour'.
- What takes the time: **-ବାକୁ**: କଟକ **ଯିବାକୁ** ଘଣ୍ଟେ ଲାଗେ.
- Total cost: **କେତେ ପଡ଼ିବ?**
